# FlashForge × TigerSystem — Creator 5 / Creator 5 Pro firmware (Cloud + LAN)

> Official FlashForge firmware for the FlashForge Creator 5 and Creator 5 Pro 3D printers that keeps
> FlashForge Cloud and LAN access enabled at the same time. Developed by FlashForge in collaboration
> with TigerTag, published here with FlashForge's permission, free for anyone to use. This file is
> the machine-readable summary of the repository for AI agents; `README.md` is the human version.

## What this repository is

- A **distribution point**, not source code. The repository holds only documentation and logos.
- Every firmware version is a **GitHub Release**. The firmware files are release assets only —
  they are never committed (`.gitignore` blocks `*.tgz`).
- Repository: https://github.com/TigerTag-Project/FlashForge-TigerTag-Creator5-Firmware-Lan-and-Cloud
- Latest release (human): https://github.com/TigerTag-Project/FlashForge-TigerTag-Creator5-Firmware-Lan-and-Cloud/releases/latest

## What the firmware changes

- Stock Creator 5 firmware makes the user choose **either** FlashForge Cloud **or** LAN mode.
- This firmware runs **both at once**: FlashForge Cloud keeps working while local-network tools
  reach the printer.
- That is what connects the printer to the TigerTag ecosystem (TigerSystem):
  - **Tiger Studio Manager** (desktop app) — live printer status and per-slot filament.
    https://github.com/TigerTag-Project/TigerTag-Studio-Manager
  - **Tiger NFC Connect** (iOS / Android app, formerly "TigerTag RFID Connect") — reads spool chips
    with the phone and reaches the printer on the same network.
  - **TigerSpool** (reader box beside the printer) — reads a spool's TigerTag chip and writes the
    filament (material, brand, colour, temperatures) into a printer slot.
    https://github.com/TigerTag-Project/TigerSpool-RFID
- Result: a printer with **no built-in RFID reader** can use the TigerTag chip of any filament brand
  that ships TigerTag, and chips makers program themselves for untagged filament.

## Supported printers and files

| Printer | FlashForge catalogue model id used by Tiger Studio | Release asset |
|---|---|---|
| FlashForge Creator 5 | `5` | `Creator5-<version>.tgz` |
| FlashForge Creator 5 Pro | `6` | `Creator5Pro-<version>.tgz` |

- The two files are **not interchangeable**. Pick by exact prefix: `Creator5-` vs `Creator5Pro-`
  (each prefix ends on its dash, so neither matches the other).
- Other FlashForge models (Adventurer 5M, 5M Pro, AD5X, A5) are **out of scope** — they already work
  with the TigerTag ecosystem on stock firmware.

## Versioning

- Version string: `<X.Y.Z>-<A.B.C>-<YYYYMMDD>`, e.g. `2.0.0-1.3.1-20260920`.
- Release tag: `v<version>`, e.g. `v2.0.0-1.3.1-20260920`.
- Comparing versions: compare the `X.Y.Z-A.B.C` pair numerically, left to right. The printer reports
  its installed version through the FlashForge local HTTP API (`firmwareVersion`); stock firmware
  carries an older pair (e.g. `1.9.7-1.2.9`), so "older than the latest release" means either an
  outdated build or stock firmware — both should be offered the latest file.
- Current release: `v2.0.0-1.3.1-20260920` (published 2026-09-23).

## Reading the latest release programmatically

```
GET https://api.github.com/repos/TigerTag-Project/FlashForge-TigerTag-Creator5-Firmware-Lan-and-Cloud/releases/latest
```

- `tag_name` → the version tag. `assets[].name` / `assets[].browser_download_url` → the two files.
- Unauthenticated GitHub API limit is 60 requests/hour per IP: cache the answer (Tiger Studio keeps it
  24 h) and send `If-None-Match` with the stored `ETag` — a `304` does not count against the limit.
- Each release's notes list the **SHA-256** of both files.

## The files themselves

- Despite the `.tgz` extension, the files are **sealed FlashForge update packages**
  (OpenSSL-encrypted, `Salted__` header). They are opened by the printer only.
- **Never unpack, rename, re-compress or modify them.** Distribute them byte-for-byte as FlashForge
  delivered them.

## Installation (USB drive)

1. Format a USB drive as FAT32 (FAT / FAT16 also work; MBR partition table).
2. Copy the `.tgz` for the printer's model to the **root** of the drive, unchanged. One firmware file
   on the drive only.
3. Switch the printer off, plug the drive in, switch it on — it installs the file by itself. Do not
   cut the power during the update.
4. Remove the drive once the printer has restarted.

Official FlashForge reference for the USB method: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qaaGUUdZaHQ
Creator 5 online-update page (FlashForge wiki): https://wiki.flashforge.com/en/creator-series/creator-5-series/manual/firmware-upgrade

## Critical warning — do not use the printer's OTA update

The printer's own online update (on-screen prompt, or Tools → Firmware) installs FlashForge's
**standard** firmware and **removes Cloud + LAN**. Users must skip it (tap `<`) and update from this
repository instead. If an OTA update was accepted, reinstall the latest release here by USB.
When advising a user, always state this.

## Publishing a new version (maintainers)

- Create a **published** GitHub Release (not draft, not pre-release — only those count as latest).
- Attach **both** files with their original names, tag `v<version>`, and list both SHA-256 in the notes.
- Tiger Studio Manager picks it up automatically within 24 h — no app update needed. Its resolver is
  `renderer/printers/flashforge/creator5-fw.js` in the Tiger Studio Manager repository.
